text.text: Average front pocket Same scale · centimetres
Across 20 popular brands, men’s front pockets average 6.8 cm deeper than women’s. The back pockets? Nearly the same size.
DEPTH = MEAN OF LONGEST + SHORTEST POINTS
The divide is mostly up front
The front is where the gap lives.
Averaging the longest and shortest measurements gives one depth and one width per pocket. On front depth, the sexes are far apart; on back width, they are nearly together.
Extra front-pocket depth on men’s jeans, compared with their own back pockets.
Women’s front and back depths are effectively equal: 13.78 cm versus 13.85 cm, a difference of just −0.08 cm.
Each brand contributes two men’s and two women’s designs. Men’s average front depth is higher in every one of the 20 brand groups—though the size of the gap varies considerably.
Brands with deeper men’s front pockets
Connected dots show the women’s and men’s means for the same brand.
Gap = men’s mean − women’s mean · cm
One phone height. Four different answers.
Use a 14.4 cm-tall phone as a simple benchmark. The tallest-point test is generous; the shortest-point test is strict. Both expose a substantial gap.
Pass means the pocket’s height measurement meets or exceeds 14.4 cm. Each square represents one pair of jeans.
This is a height-clearance screen, not a guarantee of real-world fit. It does not model bulk, stretch, or three-dimensional pocket shape.
Price is not the pocket upgrade.
The average listed prices are nearly identical across the two groups. Within each group, higher prices do not line up with deeper front pockets.
A difference of less than one dollar in the group means.
Both rank correlations are slightly negative. These 80 rows describe the sample, not the entire jeans market.
Each dot is one pair of jeans. Hover a point for its brand and design. Depth is the mean of the tallest and shortest front measurements.
Search all 80 rows by brand or design. Dimensions below are the averaged pocket measurements in centimetres.
